articles.summary: Key Takeaways AR automation isn’t one switch. It’s five separate handoffs, and a stall at any one erases the speed you won elsewhere. The gap between subscription billing and cash application does the most damage. It piles days onto DSO even when everything else runs clean. Automated invoice delivery with open tracking can lead to fewer past-due invoices, and it’s low-effort to set up. Self-service payment portals with saved methods speed collection, replacing manual chasing per account. AI cash-application matching via bank webhooks removes multi-day reconciliation lag, but it’s the hardest handoff to automate. A manual invoice runs 8–12 minutes each. Automated recurring generation from subscription data cuts issue lag to near-zero. Quick Summary Most SaaS teams treat accounts receivable automation as one big switch. It isn’t. DSO stays high because the work breaks into five separate handoffs, and a stall at any one of them undoes the speed you gained elsewhere.
articles.title: The Five Handoffs That Determine Whether AR Automation Actually Cuts DSO
